entries.evidence: The two tandem axles are built as two modules: the middle one at steps 121 to 128 (pages 78 and 79, https://www.lego.com/cdn/product-assets/product.bi.core.pdf/6208469.pdf#page=78), fitted next to the gearbox at step 139 (page 87), and the rear one at steps 143 to 151 (page 92, #page=92), fitted at the end at step 166 (page 101). The 1:1 pictures of their differentials are mirror images: in step 123 the ring is on the right of the casing, in step 147 on the left, both drawn from the same side. The file draws both alike: its two sub-models, 42070 - axle2.ldr and 42070 - axle3.ldr, hold the casing (62821) turned the same way, its ring facing +x, on the side of their red connectors. One shaft drives both, its pinions meeting the middle ring from behind and the rear ring from in front, so with both rings facing one way the two rear axles turn against each other, and the truck can't roll (function 1). Turned half a turn about the vertical, the rear casing's ring faces -x, as in step 147.

Follows from the signed entry rear-differential-ring-faces-back, which turns the rear differential's casing p845 half a turn about the vertical: the casing's small bevel gear p848 sits on the casing's own pin, inside it, and turns with it, from 17 LDU behind the casing's centre to 17 in front, as the middle differential's p758 sits in its casing p755. Left where it was, it is joined to the axle housing instead of the casing (the reading has no joint between p845 and p848), so the two side gears must turn against each other and the rear axle's wheels can't roll together: the truck can't roll straight, and the XL motor can't turn on the floor (function 1). The side gears p846 and p847 change places under the same half turn, as drawn already.
